edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 10

source_text: Adiuro vos, filiae Hierusalem, si inveneritis fratruelem meum, quid nuntietis ei? Quia amore langueo. Vox fratruelis mei; ecce iste venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles. Haec adhuc loquitur ecclesia exhortans filias Hierusalem. Amor languor fit, quando desiderium sponsi tardat. Deinde audit vocem: Ecce venit saliens in montibus — cito, potenter, per prophetas et apostolos quasi per montes et colles currens.
pass_a_gloss: I-adjure you daughters of-Jerusalem if you-find my brother what will-you-announce to-him? That with-love I-am-sick. Voice of-my brother; behold this-one comes leaping upon mountains, springing-over hills. These still speaks church exhorting daughters of-Jerusalem. Love sickness becomes when desire of-bridegroom delays. Then she-hears voice: Behold he-comes leaping upon mountains — quickly, powerfully, through prophets and apostles as through mountains and hills running.
pass_b_english: [[I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my brother, what will you tell him? That I am sick with love >> Bible:Song of Songs 5:8]]. [[The voice of my brother; behold, he comes leaping on the mountains, springing over the hills >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:8]]. The church still speaks, exhorting the daughters of Jerusalem. Love becomes a sickness when desire for the Bridegroom delays. Then she hears the voice: Behold, he comes leaping on the mountains — swiftly, powerfully, running through prophets and apostles as through mountains and hills.
notes: Song Homilia II OET; Lawson not used for wording.
